Maastricht UMC+ | Radiology | 20 January 2025 | mpMRI Prostate
Clinical context: 67-year-old man presenting with PSA 7.4 ng/mL and a previous Negative systematic biopsy.
FINDINGS:
Prostatic volume registers at 28.0 mL. A discrete abnormality occupies the right posterior mid-gland peripheral zone, spanning 14 × 10 × 12 mm. T2-weighted sequences show pronounced hypointensity against the normal peripheral zone tissue. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms marked restriction, mirrored by low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast sequences demonstrate early, focal enhancement within the same region. The transition zone remains clear of significant nodular hyperplasia. There is no evidence of seminal vesicle invasion or extraprostatic extension. Pelvic lymph nodes appear benign.
IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right posterior mid-gland peripheral zone.
prostate volume 28.0; PSA density 0.25.
csPCa probability 0.7299785.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review focused on a sustained rise in prostate-specific antigen values. An earlier measurement from September 2023 recorded 6.2 ng/mL, indicating a gradual upward trajectory. The preceding systematic biopsy yielded Negative results for malignancy. Current pharmacotherapy includes metformin and empagliflozin to manage Type 2 diabetes, with glycaemic parameters remaining stable. Recorded for specialist urological follow-up.

previous_notes.text: Annual wellness assessment conducted when the patient was 66 years old. Cardiovascular metrics showed a blood pressure reading of 138/82 mmHg.
